title: Canonical site comparisons for scalar and chart operations
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, a prime $\ell
e p$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $T,T'$, and a $k$-morphism $u:T'	o T$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A	o B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and let $N=\ell^n\ge1$ annihilate both. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use ordinary derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their comparison inverse images $
u_{T,R}^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], coefficient extension $(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and scheme inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $R=A,B$ and either site $	au$, put $R_{T,	au}(1)=\mu_{N,T}^{	au}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_{T,	au}}R_{T,	au}$, where $\mu_N$ is the sheaf of units $z$ with $z^N=1$; define $R_{T,	au}(c)$ by $c$ tensor powers, with unit for $c=0$, and $K(c)=K\otimes^L R_{T,	au}(c)$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line, lem-amb-finite-root-site-comparison]. For every bounded constructible etale $A$-complex $K$ of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-kun-tor-amplitude], there is a canonical natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$
u_{T,B}^*(K_B)\simeq(
u_{T,A}^*K)_B.$$
For $R=A,B$ and every bounded constructible etale $R$-complex $L$ of finite Tor amplitude, every $c\ge0$, and every $s\in\mathbf Z$, there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$
u_{T',R}^*(u_{\mathrm{et}}^*L)\simeq u_{\mathrm{proet}}^*(
u_{T,R}^*L),\qquad

u_{T,R}^*(L(c))\simeq(
u_{T,R}^*L)(c),\qquad

u_{T,R}^*(L[s])\simeq(
u_{T,R}^*L)[s].$$
The scalar isomorphism is induced on any flat-term K-flat representative by the ordinary balanced-tensor inverse-image comparison, with $B$ acting on the second factor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The scheme comparison is the exact localization of the usual site inverse-image square and respects identities and composites. The twist comparison is the iterated canonical tensor comparison followed by the root comparison sending each root to the same unit; it is compatible with scheme pullback, and its $c=0$ component is the constant unit identification. The shift comparison is induced by termwise inverse image and the signed differential of cochain shift. These describe the specified canonical maps, as isomorphisms in the derived categories.

proof.text: Completed lower Lean obligations: sheafified scalar extension followed by exact faithful restriction is tensoring with the constant new coefficient module. K-flat tensor acyclicity proves preservation of K-flat quasi-isomorphisms; the resolving-class derived adjunction gives pointwise left derivability. The three tensor source and target identities are reflexive and their canonical maps are invertible by the proved source-library monoidal theorem. A prime distinct from the characteristic is a unit in the field; map each power to global sections to prove modulus_isUnit. The remaining steps retain the plan for the original, still unfinished upper coherence theorem.

proof.text: Use compatible small site presentations in the coefficient universe. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], for each finite ring $R$, $\nu_{T,R}^*$ is exact and its structural map identifies the inverse image of the constant ring with the constant ring, preserving scalar sections. The analogous assertions for scheme inverse images follow from [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], applied to the geometric morphisms defining $u_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $u_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Thus these functors act termwise and preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The preservation assertion in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] shows that $\nu_{T,A}^*P$ is again flat-term K-flat. These choices compute the ordinary unbounded derived operations; bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude impose no further restriction on this argument.

Let $i_	au:(\operatorname{Sh}(T_	au),B_T)	o(\operatorname{Sh}(T_	au),A_T)$ have identity underlying topos and structural map $A_T	o B_T$. Its derived pullback is coefficient extension by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The ringed composites $i_{\mathrm{et}}
u_{T,B}$ and $
u_{T,A}i_{\mathrm{proet}}$ have the same underlying geometric inverse image and the same structural map: both send a constant $a$ to its image in $B$. The constant-ring normalization in [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] identifies these maps. Apply the composition and specified 2-isomorphism comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to these two paths. This gives $
u_{T,B}^*Li_{\mathrm{et}}^*\simeq Li_{\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_{T,A}^*$ in $D(B_{T,\mathrm{proet}})$, naturally in $K$. On the representative $P$ from Step 1 it is the ordinary map $
u_{T,B}^*(P\otimes_{A_T}B_T)	o(
u_{T,A}^*P)\otimes_{A_T}B_T$, sending the inverse image of a local tensor $x\otimes b$ to the inverse image of $x$ tensored with the same $b$. The inverse uses the reverse balanced-tensor comparison. Multiplication by $b'$ acts as $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes bb'$ on both sides, proving the required $B$-linearity. The cited composition comparison is computed on flat-term K-flat representatives, so it identifies this very map, independently of $P$, with the derived isomorphism, without requiring $B$ flat over $A$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to $u:T'\to T$. Its natural sheaf isomorphism is the usual site inverse-image square; its statement includes the identity and composition laws. The constant-module lift of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] preserves the underlying sheaf maps and their scalar operations and is exact. Hence the square acts on $R$-module complexes termwise. Naturality makes its components chain maps, and their termwise inverses are inverse chain maps. Localizing at quasi-isomorphisms gives precisely $\nu_{T',R}^*u_{\mathrm{et}}^*L\simeq u_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\nu_{T,R}^*L$. The identity and composition equations hold degree by degree before localization, hence after it. This constructs the specified comparison in the derived category, for either $R=A$ or $B$.

proof.text:
Since $\ell
e p$, $N=\ell^n$ is invertible on both schemes. For each $R$, [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] gives flat etale sheaves $R_{T,\mathrm{et}}(c)$. The isomorphism $\sigma_{N,T}$ of [lem-amb-finite-root-site-comparison] identifies $
u_{T,R}^*R_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1)$ with $R_{T,\mathrm{proet}}(1)$, sending each root to the same unit. Use the tensor and unit comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Set $\sigma_0$ equal to its constant-ring unit map. Given $\sigma_c$, define $\sigma_{c+1}$ as the tensor comparison on $R(c)\otimes_R R(1)$ followed by $\sigma_c\otimes\sigma_1$. For a flat sheaf placed in degree zero, tensor is an exact termwise functor; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] shows it carries acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes, so this degree-zero complex is K-flat. Hence flatness makes each etale tensor in this recursion ordinary; preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to these degree-zero flat complexes, makes the pro-etale tensors ordinary as well. This inductively gives $\sigma_c:
u_{T,R}^*R_{T,\mathrm{et}}(c)\simeq R_{T,\mathrm{proet}}(c)$ as derived isomorphisms. Finally compose the derived tensor comparison on $L\otimes_R^L R(c)$ with $1\otimes\sigma_c$. This is the specified natural twist isomorphism, including its unit component at $c=0$.

proof.text: For $c=1$ the scheme-pullback square for $\sigma_1$ is exactly the displayed $d^u_N,u^*\sigma,\sigma\nu^*e^u_N,\kappa_u$ equation in [lem-amb-finite-root-site-comparison]. At $c=0$ it is the unit equation for the scheme/site comparison. More explicitly, Step 3's square is a specified 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi: its module lift respects the constant structural ring maps, since both composites keep each constant scalar fixed. Thus [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] makes that square monoidal, including its unit equation. If the square commutes for $c$, tensor it with the square for $1$, and apply this monoidality equation to the recursive definition of $\sigma_{c+1}$ in Step 4. The result is the square for $c+1$. Induction proves compatibility for every $c\ge0$. Tensoring that square with the natural square for $L$, and applying the same monoidality equation, proves the claimed scheme-pullback compatibility for $L(c)$. The root maps used are the specified pullback-of-units maps, so this argument retains the normalization rather than choosing an arbitrary trivialization of a Tate line.

proof.text:
For a complex $C$, $(C[s])^i=C^{i+s}$ and $d_{C[s]}^i=(-1)^s d_C^{i+s}$, with the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Additivity and exactness of $
u_{T,R}^*$ are supplied by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Consequently $
u^*((-1)^sd)=(-1)^s
u^*(d)$. The identity on each object $
u^*C^{i+s}$ therefore gives a natural chain isomorphism $
u^*(C[s])\simeq(
u^*C)[s]$. Its localization is the required shift comparison for every integer $s$, since $
u^*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. All comparisons above were constructed before localization or through the canonical derived pullback comparisons, so their components are isomorphisms in the indicated ordinary derived categories.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact constant-ring comparison pullback; the reduction unit has no replacement for this site fact.
Generic exact lift of geometric inverse image to constant-ring modules, used on both scheme sites.
Generic flat-term K-flat resolution existence, used to identify the specified scalar representative.
Generic derived tensor comparison and flat-term K-flat preservation for ringed-topos pullback.
Generic coefficient-extension computation by K-flat resolutions; identifies the identity-topos structural ring change.
Generic normalized derived tensor, unit, composition and 2-isomorphism comparisons; needed to retain B-linearity and scheme-pullback compatibility.
Generic coherent etale/proetale sheaf inverse-image square for an arbitrary scheme map.
Generic finite-root tensor line flatness for an arbitrary finite ring annihilated by N.
Generic same-unit root comparison and its explicit arbitrary-scheme-pullback square.
Generic exact functor cohomology calculation, used to check directly that a flat sheaf in degree zero is K-flat.
